decision.summaryForCoordinator: Both v1 blockers are landed and the fold is clean. B1: the compound 'duplicate-and-concurrent' entry is replaced by two named deliveries, that string now occurs zero times, and both keep journalBytes and cleanupBound NOT-AUTHORED - so the skip I described, a fixture satisfying the corpus with a sequential duplicate alone, is no longer available. B2: all five v9 asserts are named, each verified as a verbatim substring of the live intent, at top level and identically inside both states; the two that were missing are the record-level completeness assert and the residual-versus-retry bound clause, which were exactly the two failure modes the class exists to catch. fx12Intent equals live v9 at 299 characters, the length the dispatch names, and fx12Proves is carried and exact. 5/5 cited digests recompute, and so does the v1-verdict digest the repair cites as its provenance, so the chain from finding to fix is verifiable. I checked two deltas that could have been quiet regressions and neither is: removing v1's three boolean asserts is correct because an input corpus should not pre-judge outcomes, and the uniform assertsNamedNotAuthored list is the fx5 v2 convention the remedy pointed at; and swapping 'CLN record bytes' for 'a journal envelope' increases coverage rather than reducing it. One thing on the record: the two deliveryNamed strings reproduce my own remedy wording verbatim, so their exactness is compliance rather than independent derivation - the substance behind them checks out against v9 independently. FX-12 v1 is also the first failure in this stretch that was not a truncated quotation, so sweeping FX-10 and FX-11 for the truncation defect alone would not clear them. 16 attacks run, 16 refuted.
